summary: Sporting News' Bill Bender assesses winners and losers after the Big Ten barred Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh from the sideline for the rest of the regular season over the in-person scouting and sign-stealing scandal tied to staffer Connor Stalions. Winners include commissioner Tony Petitti, Ohio State-Michigan TV ratings, helmet communication technology and interim coach Sherrone Moore; losers include Stalions, Harbaugh and the Big Ten. Michigan's fate remains undetermined as the NCAA investigation continues.
one_line: After the Big Ten suspended Jim Harbaugh from the sideline, Bender ranks winners and losers of Michigan's sign-stealing scandal, from Tony Petitti to Connor Stalions.
key_facts: The Big Ten announced Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh is prohibited from coaching on the sideline for the remainder of the regular season, though he can coach during the week.
Staffer Connor Stalions resigned on Nov. 3 amid an NCAA investigation into Michigan for in-person scouting and sign stealing.
Michigan beat No. 10 Penn State 24-15 under interim coach Sherrone Moore, rushing for 227 yards including 32 straight run plays.
Michigan did not get a ruling on a temporary restraining order before the Penn State game; Harbaugh's TRO hearing is set for Nov. 17.
The Big Ten says it has not linked Harbaugh to any wrongdoing and that the penalty is institutional; the NCAA investigation continues.
Last year's Ohio State-Michigan game drew an 8.05 Nielsen rating with 17.1 million viewers; Harbaugh is 2-5 and Ohio State coach Day is 1-2 in the rivalry.
The NCAA rules committee is giving teams the option of coach-to-player helmet communication during bowl season, per CBSSports.com on Oct. 20.
ESPN.com reported Stalions allegedly bought tickets to more than 35 games involving Big Ten and potential CFP opponents.
Harbaugh is 31-3, and Michigan is 35-3, since the program bottomed out at the end of the 2020 season.

Bender calls this the Big Ten's fourth football scandal in less than a calendar year, following Iowa betting, Pat Fitzgerald's July 10 firing at Northwestern and Mel Tucker's Sept. 27 firing at Michigan State.
Michigan countered with allegations that Ohio State and Rutgers leaked its signs to Purdue in last year's Big Ten championship game.
Michigan is 10-0 with a defense allowing 7.5 points per game, and still faces Maryland and No. 1 Ohio State.
The Big Ten welcomes four new members next season: Oregon, UCLA, USC and Washington.
